Write a model as a NONMEM control stream

Source: R/write-nonmem.R
pmx_write_nonmem.Rd

Prints a model as an NM-TRAN control stream with its fidelity (see pmx_fidelity()).

Usage

pmx_write_nonmem(model, estimates = c("final", "initial"))

Arguments

model

A model read by one of the pmx_read_*() functions.

estimates

"final" writes final estimates where the model has them, and its initial values elsewhere; "initial" writes initial values. Whichever of the two is not written is recorded as lost.

Value

A written model: the text as lines, its fidelity and its losses.

Details

Fixed effects become THETA(n), random effects ETA(n) and residual errors EPS(n), numbered in the model's order; compartment amounts become A(n). A closed form is written as its ADVAN/TRANS pair, an ODE model as ADVAN13 with $MODEL and $DES. Residual error held as standard deviations, as rxode2 holds it, is written as $SIGMA variances: the same model, parameterised as NONMEM parameterises it.

$INPUT and $DATA are placeholders to point at a dataset, and no $ESTIMATION is written: the representation holds neither.

Examples

corpus <- zupkpmx_corpus()
fun <- eval(parse(file.path(corpus$path[[1]], "model-rxode2.R")))
pmx_write_nonmem(pmx_read_rxode2(fun))
#> $PROBLEM zupkpmx model read from rxode2
#> ; zupkpmx: $INPUT and $DATA are placeholders; point them at your dataset.
#> $INPUT ID TIME EVID AMT RATE CMT DV
#> $DATA data.csv IGNORE=@
#> $SUBROUTINES ADVAN2 TRANS2
#> $PK
#> KA = THETA(1)
#> CL = THETA(2) * EXP(ETA(1))
#> V = THETA(3) * EXP(ETA(2))
#> S2 = V
#> $ERROR
#> Y = F * (1 + EPS(1))
#> $THETA (0, 1) ; tka
#> $THETA (0, 4) ; tcl
#> $THETA (0, 50) ; tv
#> $OMEGA 0.09
#> $OMEGA 0.09
#> $SIGMA 0.04
#> # nonmem, fidelity: equivalent
